Let \(R=\mathbb F_2[t]/(t^3)\). An object of \(\mathcal C\) is just a finite free \(R\)-module, with \(t\) acting as \(N\). Thus \(X_n\simeq R^n\), and natural endomorphisms of \(U^{\oplus 6}\) are exactly \(6\times 6\) matrices over \(R\).

Write
\[
P=\Pi=\begin{pmatrix}I_3&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
E=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\ C&D\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
EP-PE=\begin{pmatrix}0&B\\ C&0\end{pmatrix},
\]
so on \(X_n\simeq R^n\) its \(\mathbb F_2\)-rank is
\[
n\bigl(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_2}B+\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_2}C\bigr).
\]

The maximum possible rank is \(18n\), requiring both \(B,C\) invertible over \(R\). If \(B\) is invertible, the idempotent equations force
\[
D=I+B^{-1}AB,\qquad C=DB^{-1}A.
\]
Hence \(C\) is invertible iff \(A\) and \(I+A\) are invertible. Over the local ring \(R\), this depends only on reduction mod \(t\). In \(M_3(\mathbb F_2)\), matrices \(A_0\) with both \(A_0\) and \(I+A_0\) invertible are exactly the \(48\) elements of order \(7\) in \(\mathrm{GL}_3(\mathbb F_2)\). Each has \(2^{18}\) lifts to \(R\), and
\[
|\mathrm{GL}_3(R)|=|\mathrm{GL}_3(\mathbb F_2)|2^{18}=168\cdot 2^{18}.
\]
Thus
\[
N_n^{(1)}=(168\cdot 2^{18})(48\cdot 2^{18})
=8064\cdot 2^{36}.
\]

For the second largest rank, the only possibility is \(17n\): one of \(B,C\) is invertible and the other has \(\mathbb F_2\)-rank \(8\). By symmetry, count the case \(B\) invertible and double it.

With \(B\) invertible, after replacing \(A\) by \(B^{-1}AB\), we need
\[
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_2}\bigl(A(I+A)\bigr)=8.
\]
Modulo \(t\), this requires \(A_0(I+A_0)\) to have rank \(2\). The possible rational canonical types over \(\mathbb F_2\) are:
\[
J_3(0),\quad J_3(1),\quad [0]\oplus C_{x^2+x+1},\quad [1]\oplus C_{x^2+x+1}.
\]
Their conjugacy class sizes are
\[
42,\ 42,\ 56,\ 56,
\]
so there are \(196\) such reductions. For each such \(A_0\), exactly half of the \(2^9\) choices of the \(t\)-coefficient lift make the determinant have valuation exactly \(1\), and the \(t^2\)-coefficient is arbitrary. Hence the number of \(A\) with rank \(8\) is
\[
196\cdot 2^8\cdot 2^9=196\cdot 2^{17}.
\]
Therefore
\[
N_n^{(2)}=2(168\cdot 2^{18})(196\cdot 2^{17})
=32928\cdot 2^{36}.
\]

So for every \(n\ge 1\),
\[
\boxed{
\left(R_n^{(1)},N_n^{(1)},R_n^{(2)},N_n^{(2)}\right)
=
\left(18n,\ 8064\cdot 2^{36},\ 17n,\ 32928\cdot 2^{36}\right).
}
\]
